text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
-- Officials of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) said in Budapest that Hungary's economic performance may have improved but the population's state of health is not better.
-- The Finance Ministry plans to reduce personal income tax rates next year.
-- The tax authority APEH plans to survey individuals' revenues other than wages but the ombudsman for data protection has raised objections to the forms planned to be used.

-- The Welfare Ministry said it hoped that persons who are responsible for law breaches at the social security in the past few years will not be reelected into the governing bodies of the social security.
